purpose: Make concepts, steps, state changes, comparisons and repair feedback visible through a type-appropriate representation without turning visual decoration, page activity or AI output into mastery evidence.

principles.rule: A visual declares a learning role, observable change and evidence relationship; decorative media never satisfies a required learning block or Master-ready stage.
Shared state and feedback semantics do not replace formula, language, code, database, architecture, ML, system or research renderers owned by specialist engines.
A visual teaching sequence may render inline, as a stepper, deck, split view, workspace, modal or external artifact and never implies a fixed tab count.
Interactive visuals require a learner purpose: predict, manipulate or construct, observe a state change, and explain or record the result.
Feedback exposes one primary diagnosed error group at a time, links it to a source and recovery action, and keeps secondary findings available without flooding the learner.
Practice and formal assessment use separate disclosure policies; protected correctness, hints and solutions remain hidden until the applicable submission boundary.
Color, motion, sound, geometry or pointer input is never the only carrier of meaning; every representation has an equivalent perceivable and operable fallback.
Previously available visuals, learner actions, deterministic feedback, reset and repair remain usable offline without generative AI.
Provided visual sources, learner actions, deterministic state and AI interpretation remain distinguishable and versioned.

visualEnvelope.identityRule: visualId is stable within a versioned lesson source and never derives only from array position or current DOM order.
visualEnvelope.blockRule: blockRef resolves a Universal Lesson block; a visual does not create a hidden parallel lesson structure.
visualEnvelope.sourceRule: sourceBindings reuse the Universal Lesson source binding contract and preserve authoritative specialist artifact precedence.
visualEnvelope.specialistCapabilityRule: specialistCapabilityRef is required as an explicit field but may be null when the registered family renderer preserves the full learning meaning; otherwise it resolves to a capability registered for the lesson type.
visualEnvelope.evidenceRule: evidenceRefs identify observable learner artifacts or events; opening, viewing or animating a visual alone is not evidence.

families.annotated-illustration: An image, formula surface or media frame with source-grounded labels and a non-image description.
families.relationship-diagram: Nodes, edges, boundaries or traceability links with explicit semantics and a structured text or table fallback.
families.step-sequence: An ordered reasoning or construction path whose steps have stable identity and observable transitions.
families.state-comparison: Two or more states compared by named dimensions, including partial or inconclusive outcomes when the domain is not binary.
families.trace-timeline: An ordered execution, dialogue, transaction, protocol or lifecycle trace with keyboard-readable events.
families.plot-or-chart: A quantitative display with units, scale, series meaning and accessible underlying data.
families.media-overlay: Audio, video, handwriting or image media synchronized with transcript, captions, annotations or timing state.
families.artifact-view: A versioned learner or source artifact preview that preserves provenance and does not silently copy private local bytes.
families.interactive-model: A deterministic parameterized model with initial state, controls, observable outputs, reset and reproducibility metadata.
families.specialist-widget: A registered subject-engine tool used when a generic family cannot preserve the domain interaction.

fallbackOrder: deterministic static state or artifact snapshot
representationContract.resolutionRule: Resolve lessonType, then a registered representationKind, then its family and specialist capability; never infer a renderer from an arbitrary file extension alone.
representationContract.profileUsageRule: A type profile is an allowed typed vocabulary and compatibility target; an individual lesson instantiates only visuals justified by its objectives and block policy and never all profile kinds by default.
representationContract.noGenericReplacementRule: A fallback preserves learning meaning but does not claim feature parity with a missing formula, dialogue, code, query, diagram, simulation or research tool.

transitions.when: prerequisite or recovery requirement is satisfied
learner explicitly starts or resumes the step
the required learner action is committed
an authorized deterministic evaluator or instructor verifies the step evidence
a diagnosed error or missing evidence blocks the step
the learner follows the source-linked repair and retries
required explanation or evidence capture for the step is committed

rules: Step gating applies to the learning sequence, never to a fixed UI tab count.
A locked step exposes why it is locked and a reachable prerequisite or recovery route.
Reset restores a documented initial state without deleting append-only learner evidence.
The current step, controls and state change remain understandable at mobile, tablet and desktop widths.
State labels and icons accompany color; focus moves only after an explicit learner action.
Correct and incorrect states identify the governing dimension, not only a green or red surface.
Non-binary technical results may be partially-correct, inconclusive or needs-review.
A runtime error, unavailable source and incorrect learner answer are separate states.
An incorrect comparison names one primary cause and a source-linked repair before retry.
Formal assessment never exposes per-item correctness before the submission boundary.
correctWrongContract.nullableReferenceRule: repairRef may be null for correct or unattempted outcomes; it is required for partially-correct, incorrect and needs-review outcomes.

determinismRules: The same versioned inputs, parameters and seed reproduce the same deterministic output.
Run, pause, step, retry and reset behavior is explicit when supported.
A required interaction has a keyboard-operable path and a non-pointer fallback.
Autoplay never performs a learner action or creates mastery evidence.
An interaction records stable event and artifact references rather than an opaque screenshot alone.

feedbackContract.primaryErrorRule: primaryErrorRef may be null for correct or unscored feedback; it is required when feedback creates a needs-repair route.
rules: Feedback states what changed, why it matters, where the governing source is and what one action to retry.
Praise or warning without observable state evidence is not sufficient feedback.
AI advisory feedback cannot set verified, fabricate a source or reveal a protected assessment answer.
Unavailable AI falls back to deterministic rules, source anchors and the registered recovery route.
A repaired attempt appends a link to prior evidence and never rewrites history.

formal-assessment.protectedAnswerRule: Per-item correctness, protected hints and solutions are unavailable to learner and AI advisory before submission.

plot-or-chart: axis units scale and series description
artifact-view: download or reader fallback when authorized

responsiveRules: No required label, control, legend or feedback is clipped at supported mobile, tablet or desktop widths.
A split view may stack while preserving source-before-action reading order.
Zoom and text reflow do not require two-dimensional scrolling for the surrounding lesson shell.
Motion pauses and reduced-motion mode preserves the same learning state.

rules: Core instructions, deterministic controls, outcome rules and text or table fallback remain available offline.
Large visual or media packs require explicit download and are never silently precached as the whole subject repository.
Direct Local Reader artifacts stay zero-copy and permission scoped; the visual contract stores references, not private file bytes.
Missing cloud or AI service never blocks practice, assessment, progress, review or deterministic repair.
A stale or failed visual resource reports its own availability state without being mislabeled as an incorrect learner answer.
Specialist widgets and large media lazy-load at the point of use.
The lesson reserves stable layout space before a visual loads.
Animation and simulation pause when hidden and do not run solely for decoration.
A static or structured fallback renders before an optional large pack is available.
B6 defines metadata and behavior; numeric runtime budgets remain owned by performance gates and measured devices.

domainRules: Pronunciation feedback separates transcript similarity from verified language competence.
Listening visuals keep transcript timing and an offline non-audio recovery path.
Correct-wrong phrase comparison explains meaning, form or pronunciation dimension rather than color alone.
Formula and derivation visuals preserve assumptions, notation, dimensions and source anchors.
Plots expose axis scale, units, parameter state and underlying values.
A simulation requires prediction before manipulation when prediction is the learning objective.
Code state binds source version, input, runtime and deterministic test output.
A trace never substitutes animation for readable source line, stack and variable state.
Test diffs focus the first causal failure while keeping the complete log retrievable.
Schema visuals preserve keys, cardinality, optionality and integrity constraints in the fallback table.
Query-plan comparison binds the exact schema, query, statistics assumptions and engine version.
Transaction timelines distinguish isolation anomaly, runtime failure and incorrect learner prediction.
Every design visual identifies viewpoint, boundary, element semantics and traceable requirements.
Correctness may be conditional on a quality-attribute scenario and is not reduced to one canonical picture.
Diagram repair preserves prior versions and records the defended tradeoff.
Metric visuals bind dataset split, baseline, uncertainty and evaluation version.
A high score never hides leakage, invalid evaluation or an unsupported comparison.
Confusion matrices and error slices expose counts, labels and underlying scoped examples when authorized.
System visuals declare boundary, actors, information flow, assumptions and operating state.
Reliability and failure representations distinguish probability, observed event and learner hypothesis.
Lifecycle and ergonomic comparisons name the scenario and criteria that govern the judgment.
Claim-source visuals keep provided source, learner note, system-derived relation and AI inference separate.
Result plots preserve method, sample, units, uncertainty, limitations and versioned source data.
НИР/ВКР milestone state records evidence and review status without treating a decorative progress bar as completion.

kept: one primary error at a time

forwardOwnership.L6-B7: Russian Twin and English Research Layer hooks
forwardOwnership.L6-B8: machine-readable lesson schema and version migration
forwardOwnership.L6-B9: Subject Factory registry and specialist widget registration
forwardOwnership.L6-B10: Universal Lesson Renderer and legacy bridges
forwardOwnership.rule: B6 defines semantics and validation inputs; it does not claim that a universal renderer, subject mapping or legacy projection already exists.

rollback.scope: Remove the B6 contract, decision record, generated report and workflow gate, then restore progress markers to the B5 checkpoint.
